description: List ads in an ad set, or across the whole ad account when adSetId is omitted. To find ads by name without knowing their ad set, omit adSetId and pass search (name contains); each row then includes adsetId, adsetName, campaignId and campaignName. status defaults to 'active', so pass 'all' to include paused ads. To see why ads were rejected or have delivery issues, add reviewFeedback and/or issues to fields (Meta's policy reasons and issues_info); they are read only when named in fields. Returns one bounded page; follow paging.after for more. Use fields to return only the columns you need; large pages are trimmed to fit the output budget.

adSetId.description: Meta ad set ID. Omit to list ads across the whole ad account, e.g. to find ads by name with search when the ad set is unknown; each row then includes adsetName, campaignId and campaignName.

after.description: Opaque paging.after cursor. Keep filters unchanged.

fields.description: Return only these output columns. id is always returned. status is the configured state; effectiveStatus is the effective delivery state. Either is null when Meta does not provide it. adsetName, campaignId and campaignName are returned only when adSetId is omitted. reviewFeedback (Meta's rejection reasons) and issues (delivery issues) are read only when named here; omitting fields does not include them. Omit for all other columns; an empty array returns only id.

fresh.description: Accepted for compatibility; this list always reads fresh data.

offset.description: Offset within the fetched results. Requests fetch up to 500 rows. After budget trimming, use pagination.nextOffset with the same input after; consume remaining rows before following paging.after.

search.description: Optional ad name search text (name contains). Works with or without adSetId.

status.description: Exact 'active' filters active/in-process delivery states (default); other values mean no status filter on existing campaign and parent-scoped lists. Without a parent ID, account-wide lists also support 'inactive' (non-active, excluding deleted) and 'archived' (archived only).
